title: Two new tech documentaries you really need to see
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: Surveilled
recommendations.blurb: First, read Ronan Farrow’s latest New Yorker article about how the US government could very easily hack your tech. Then watch this new doc about how this kind of thing is happening all over the world, and Farrow won’t seem so dramatic when he basically advocates hucking your phone out the window.

recommendations.name: Buy Now! The Shopping Conspiracy
recommendations.blurb: This looks like it belongs in the legacy of The Great Hack and The Social Dilemma, which is to say, very alarming and somewhat overstated documentaries about how the world really works.

recommendations.name: Teenage Engineering’s OP-XY
recommendations.blurb: The OP-1 is still Teenage Engineering’s classic and most iconic synthesizer, but this new synthesizer / sampler / sequencer looks like an even more powerful portable music maker. TE is maybe the only company that makes me wish I were a musician, just so I’d have a reason to buy this.

recommendations.name: Dune: Prophecy
recommendations.blurb: My obsession with all things Dune is not a secret if you’ve been reading Installer for a while. So far, this super-prequel isn’t exactly fizzing with action, but it’s dramatic and big and I’m into it.

recommendations.name: Year of the Ring
recommendations.blurb: Our friends over at Polygon put together this epic tale about an epic tale: Lord of the Rings. Stories about the books, the movies, the characters, the fanfiction, and so much more. If you’re a Tolkien-head, you won’t want to miss this.

recommendations.name: Queue
recommendations.blurb: A perfectly minimalist iPhone podcast app, this one. You add a show, it puts new episodes in a list, you play things from the list. The more I use it, the more I wonder why any podcast app does anything else.

recommendations.name: Tokyo Override
recommendations.blurb: Intense commentary about capitalism, fascism, AI, and the surveillance state, dressed up in a stylishly animated story about hackers riding motorcycles in futuristic Tokyo? Extremely into it.

recommendations.name: The Amazon Echo Show 21
recommendations.blurb: I’m sorry, but a 21-inch “smart display” is just a TV. But I think Amazon’s idea with these new, bigger Echo devices — which is basically to have one giant screen as the hub of your smart home — is the right one.

recommendations.name: One Billion Users
recommendations.blurb: The folks at Techdirt have a surprisingly strong hit rate for fun games. I bought their CIA card game a while back and played the heck out of Startup Trail. This one’s a card game about starting a social network, and it’ll be a hit at my Thanksgiving one of these years.

recommendations.name: The JVC HA-NP1T “Nearphones”
recommendations.blurb: Another cool-looking set of open-ear headphones, which let you hear your music and the world around you. And unlike so many others, these don’t cost a fortune! A hundred bucks, in that dark green color, sounds like my kind of thing.

recommendations.name: IMG_0001
recommendations.blurb: A few weeks ago, Ben Wallace found a trove of videos on YouTube that had been uploaded directly from iPhones a dozen years ago or so. Riley Walz went and compiled 5 million of the videos, and they’re both incredibly mundane and often weirdly intimate?

recommendations.name: I typically carry three phones with me
recommendations.blurb: The phone: I typically carry three phones with me... my primary SIM is in an iPhone, then I usually have the latest Samsung and Pixel for reference.

recommendations.name: Backdrops
recommendations.blurb: I always get it from the app Backdrops.

recommendations.name: YouTube Music
recommendations.blurb: I recently switched to YouTube Music from Spotify because it’s included in my YouTube Premium membership.

recommendations.name: Notion
recommendations.blurb: I have tried every single note-taking app in the world, and Notion actually seems to do a majority of the stuff I like.

recommendations.name: Microsoft To Do
recommendations.blurb: There are two things I like about Microsoft To Do: you can start each day fresh with a fresh list just for that day, and you can attach a file to your to-do items.

recommendations.name: Email Me
recommendations.blurb: On iPhone, I love Email Me, and on Android, I just found a new app to replace my old one, also called EmailMe, but not from the same developer.

recommendations.name: EmailMe
recommendations.blurb: On iPhone, I love Email Me, and on Android, I just found a new app to replace my old one, also called EmailMe, but not from the same developer.

recommendations.name: ElevenReader
recommendations.blurb: I’m really trying to find a better way for that system, but I love how ElevenReader can read articles to me while I’m at the gym if I want to brush up on things before my radio show.

recommendations.name: Claude
recommendations.blurb: My preferred AI is Claude.

recommendations.name: Whisper Memos
recommendations.blurb: A couple of other apps that I absolutely love: one is an iOS app called Whisper Memos.

recommendations.name: Voicenotes
recommendations.blurb: Another is called Voicenotes: it’s more of a digital voice notebook.

recommendations.name: That ‘90s Show
recommendations.blurb: I mostly watch when I’m traveling — right now, I’m bingeing That ‘90s Show, which I find easy to digest and silly.

recommendations.name: Teddy Wayne
recommendations.blurb: Right now, I’m really into the author Teddy Wayne.

recommendations.name: The Winner
recommendations.blurb: I loved his book The Winner and have been reading his older stuff.

recommendations.name: T.J. Newman
recommendations.blurb: Because of my wild work schedule (I work early mornings, so I don’t have the typical downtime at night to just watch some TV), I rarely watch TV shows or movies. I mostly watch when I’m traveling — right now, I’m bingeing That ‘90s Show, which I find easy to digest and silly.

recommendations.name: Techmeme Ride Home
recommendations.blurb: As for podcasts, I always listen to Techmeme Ride Home each morning (ironically on my way to work) and check Techmeme in general about a gazillion times a day.

recommendations.name: Techmeme
recommendations.blurb: As for podcasts, I always listen to Techmeme Ride Home each morning (ironically on my way to work) and check Techmeme in general about a gazillion times a day.

recommendations.name: SnowFall
recommendations.blurb: A new timed crossword puzzle game called SnowFall. Love how it takes the elements of a crossword puzzle and throws them at you one at a time. Builds a little anxiety to the unlimited time of a traditional crossword. Starts easy but gets hard fast.

recommendations.name: Silo
recommendations.blurb: Deep in Apple TV Plus this past couple weeks. Silo is back, and the second season of Bad Sisters continues to be compelling TV. Small screen rules going into the holidays.

recommendations.name: Bad Sisters
recommendations.blurb: Deep in Apple TV Plus this past couple weeks. Silo is back, and the second season of Bad Sisters continues to be compelling TV. Small screen rules going into the holidays.

recommendations.name: Cooked
recommendations.blurb: Cooked has been a huge help turning my ever-growing collection of social media recipes into something actually usable.

recommendations.name: Thunderbird
recommendations.blurb: I switched to Thunderbird on my Pixel device, and it is better IMO than the Gmail app. My biggest complaint with the Gmail app was not being able to see if my other accounts have emails without fully switching over to them.

recommendations.name: Razer Wolverine
recommendations.blurb: Trying to decide if I want to splurge on the new Razer Wolverine. It’s finally wireless for Xbox, but then the question becomes whether I can tolerate the software on PC. It’s been fascinating finally seeing wireless Xbox controllers from other brands.

recommendations.name: Milo Rossi
recommendations.blurb: Learning about the fascinating and morbid history of vampire burials with the hilarious Milo Rossi!

recommendations.name: Sill
recommendations.blurb: Sill, by Tyler Fisher, is a new tool that connects to your Bluesky and / or Mastodon accounts, collecting all links posted to your timeline and displaying the most popular ones in your network. It’s similar to Nuzzel for Twitter and free to use.

recommendations.name: KarmaZoo
recommendations.blurb: Lately, I’ve been really into KarmaZoo, a unique little multiplayer puzzle platformer that features you, as a cute little pixel animal, wordlessly teaming up with a bunch of other player-animals — each with their own special abilities — to navigate levels as a team.

recommendations.name: Vehicle Motion Cues
recommendations.blurb: Vehicle Motion Cues on iOS to do two things: 1) Prevent motion sickness using the phone while riding in a car and 2) Remind myself that I should not use my phone while riding in a car.

recommendations.name: 3-in-1 chargers from Anker
recommendations.blurb: I bought a couple of these 3-in-1 chargers from Anker for traveling, and I love them so much. My fiance can never remember to bring both of his cords to charge his phone and his watch when we travel, so I’m very excited.

recommendations.name: Interstellar in 70mm IMAX
recommendations.blurb: I’m excited that I scored tickets to see Interstellar in 70mm IMAX for its 10th anniversary. It’s one of my favorite movies of all time, and I just happen to live by one of the few theaters that can play it in 70mm. I’m pumped!

recommendations.name: Doppler
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been getting back into listening to music I actually own. It’s tough to find an aesthetic and useful FLAC-compatible music player on the Mac, but Doppler has been filling that role pretty well. A simple interface and Last.fm scrobbling are my favorite features.

recommendations.name: Reeder
recommendations.blurb: Reeder just added Bluesky account integration! Now, it has Mastodon, Bluesky, YouTube, RSS, podcasts… It is slowly becoming my first and only app open!

recommendations.name: Us Weekly’ s full guide to the season
recommendations.blurb: I have Us Weekly’ s full guide to the season bookmarked in my browser, and I am only slightly ashamed to admit that I just signed up for Hallmark Plus.
